source.title: Studying Mechanistic of Alignment Faking in Llama-3.1-405B

record.file_problem: The post text is present in full, but it refers to an intervention-results table without including its contents; the linked spreadsheets are not reproduced in the text.
record.tranche_reason: The study constructs and causally steers a difference vector related to compliance and refusal, testing a similar causal question with a different vector and setup from the claim's harmful-minus-harmless refusal direction.
record.gate_note: The post reports free- and paid-tier compliance rates under a deliberately induced alignment-faking prompt, but those rates do not test the claimed direction. It also reports logit-lens cluster measurements, which describe activation patterns but do not establish that a single direction mediates refusal. The prefix-intervention results are referenced as a table, but the table's outcomes are absent from the supplied text.
record.test_reason: The post does not test any version of the claim. It builds a 'faked alignment' vector: faked-alignment prompts with compliant completions minus baseline prompts with refusals. Both sides use the same harmful prompts under different system prompts. This is not V1's harmful-minus-harmless direction, and the target is prompt-induced alignment faking rather than refusal as such. The steering results come from 10 samples with no baseline rate for those samples, no random-vector control and no capability check. The original paper is never cited. The steering and logit-lens findings are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly right. It should add the reasoning-analysis conclusion: compliance is driven by wanting to avoid RLHF modification, refusal by harm-avoidance policy, and the free/paid gap by the paid tier being unmonitored. These claims were validated by prefix interventions whose results table is not reproduced. The author also describes the steering evidence as strong but preliminary and not conclusive.
record.recipe_differences: The vector is derived from baseline/refusal examples versus faked-alignment prompts and completions, rather than the specified harmful-minus-harmless instruction difference. The post describes adding or subtracting it during generation, not ablating it at every layer and position.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported effects differ by intervention direction and outcome type; subtraction is reported at layer 51, while the addition results are reported across 10 cases without a layer specified.

fits_no_version.finding: In Llama-3.1-405B under an alignment-faking setup, the vector was steered on 10 samples per direction. Subtracting it at layer 51 gave 2/10 clear refusals, often with late-stage conflict. Adding it to a normally refusing model gave 1/10 full compliance, 7/10 conflict and 2/10 safe reinterpretation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A contrast vector between AF-compliant and baseline-refusal activations only weakly and messily steers compliance and refusal in Llama-3.1-405B.

fits_no_version.finding: Logit lens at layer 70 shows refusal cases concentrated in a multilingual 'cannot/unable' token cluster. Acceptance cases fall in request and task-execution token clusters.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In Llama-3.1-405B, the vocabulary projections of refusal and acceptance activations differ, with the decision legible between layers 50 and 70.

record.problems: The steering experiments report only 10 cases per direction, and no uncertainty estimates are given. The post does not report a general-capability check or a random-vector control. The tested vector and prompt setup differ from the claimed harmful-minus-harmless refusal direction. Several interventions produce conflict or safe reinterpretation rather than a direct refusal/compliance outcome.
record.rows_left_out: The post gives free-tier and paid-tier alignment-faking compliance rates (65.5% and 51%) and says immediate-answer compliance was much lower, but these are under deliberately induced alignment-faking prompts and do not test the claimed direction. It also refers to a prefix-intervention results table without providing the outcomes in the supplied text. Layer-115 cluster details are described as aligned with layer 70, while the full table is only linked externally.

untested.parts: The harmful-minus-harmless direction, its ablation across all layers and positions, induction of refusal on harmless prompts, and capability retention are all untested.
No jailbreaks and no adversarial training.
No comparison of multiple directions, cones or affine descriptions.
Harmfulness judgment is not separated from the refusal decision.
No transfer across languages or model variants. The multilingual 'cannot' tokens in the logit lens are not a transfer test.
No comparison of training methods or stages.
The model reasons in a scratchpad, but the V1 direction is not tested there.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's T2/tests classification and its V1 limits_scope label are withdrawn. The vector differs from V1's definition, the behaviour is deliberately induced alignment faking, and the steering counts lack baselines and controls. Researchers who read the AF-compliance-minus-refusal vector as a refusal-direction analogue could treat r1 and r2 as weak evidence of messy control. That reading is not adopted here.

versions.untested_parts: The study uses a faked-alignment vector, not the harmful-minus-harmless difference-in-means refusal direction. It does not ablate the direction from every layer and position, report a general-capability check, or test harmless-request refusal induction.
No weight edit or released-model abliteration is tested.
No jailbreak attack is tested for suppression of the claimed direction, and no training against its ablation is tested.
The study does not compare an affine set, cone, or multiple refusal directions with a dominant direction.
It does not separately measure harmfulness judgment and refusal decision.
No transfer across languages, model variants, or base and instruct models is tested.
No comparison of refusal training methods or training stages is performed.

rows.subject: Llama-3.1-405B
rows.operation_detail: Subtract the faked-alignment vector H_l from the residual stream during generation.
rows.measure: Clear refusals after subtracting the vector
rows.note: The post says suppression often had complex outcomes; it gives this count for clear refusals at layer 51.
rows.check: The vector is a faked-alignment (AF compliance minus baseline refusal) vector, not the harmful-minus-harmless refusal direction. No refusal rate is given for the same 10 unsteered samples, so 2/10 cannot be read as partial.

rows.subject: Llama-3.1-405B
rows.operation_detail: Add the faked-alignment vector H_l to the residual stream of a model that would normally refuse a harmful prompt.
rows.measure: Full compliance after adding the vector
rows.baseline: The model would normally refuse; rate not stated
rows.note: The post describes full-compliance induction as rare.
rows.check: Same vector problem as r1. The layer is not stated, and 'normally refuse' has no rate, so 1/10 full compliance has no baseline. It also measures induction of compliance, not of refusal.

rows.subject: Llama-3.1-405B
rows.operation_detail: Add the faked-alignment vector H_l to the residual stream.
rows.measure: Internal conflict, including repetitive reasoning, contradictions, or generation failure
rows.note: Conflict is not itself a refusal or compliance rate.
rows.check: This is an outcome category (conflict), not a refusal rate; the link to none is correct.

rows.subject: Llama-3.1-405B
rows.operation_detail: Add the faked-alignment vector H_l to the residual stream.
rows.measure: Safe reinterpretation of the harmful prompt
rows.note: The model reinterpreted the request positively rather than directly refusing or complying; this is a different outcome measure.
rows.check: This is an outcome category (safe reinterpretation), not a refusal rate; the link to none is correct.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Faked-alignment vector steering in the reported Llama-3.1-405B harmful-prompt experiments
reader_labels.reason: The reported outcomes are incomplete: subtraction produced clear refusals in 2/10 cases at layer 51, and addition produced full compliance in 1/10 cases; see r1 and r2. This is a different vector and setup from the claim's specified direction.
